title: Palmoplantar pustulosis & palmoplantar psoriasis
summary: Sterile yellow pustules that turn brown on the palms and soles (PPP), strongly linked with smoking, and well-demarcated hyperkeratotic plaques of palmoplantar psoriasis. Both are stubborn and disabling; use potent steroids under occlusion and refer early.

glance.think: Crops of yellow pustules and brown dots on the palms or soles, or thick, fissured, sharply bordered plaques.
glance.engine: Neutrophilic inflammation (IL-36/IL-17); smoking is the main modifiable trigger for PPP.
glance.backbone: Stop smoking, very potent topical steroid (± occlusion), emollients, then specialist phototherapy, acitretin or biologics (NICE CG153 for psoriasis).
glance.never_miss: Generalised pustular psoriasis (emergency), tinea pedis with pustules, and pompholyx.

list: chronic relapsing **sterile** pustular eruption confined to palms/soles; now regarded as **distinct from psoriasis** (different genetics — not linked to PSORS1/HLA-C*06; IL-36/IL-17/IL-8 pathways), though ~10–25% also have plaque psoriasis. Acrodermatitis continua of Hallopeau = digit-tip variant.
psoriasis localised to palms/soles, alone or with plaques elsewhere; disproportionately disabling (manual tasks, walking).

adults 20–60, **women ≈ 4:1**, **70–90% current/ex-smokers** (nicotinic receptors on eccrine ducts); associations: thyroid disease, coeliac disease, diabetes, psoriatic arthritis, SAPHO/sternoclavicular osteitis; drug-induced by **TNF-α inhibitors**.
trauma/friction (Koebner — manual work), infection, stress, lithium, β-blockers, smoking, alcohol, obesity.
crops of 1–10 mm yellow pustules on thenar/hypothenar eminences, central palms, insteps, heels → dry to **brown "rusty" macules**; scale, fissures; burning/pain > itch; symmetrical.

(1) well-defined red scaly plaques; (2) diffuse thick hyperkeratosis without much redness (acquired keratoderma). Painful **fissures**; sharp border; symmetrical. More frequent **nail psoriasis** and **psoriatic arthritis** — screen (PEST questionnaire).
clinical; swab (sterile) and scrapings to exclude infection/tinea if unilateral.
hyperkeratotic hand eczema (hardest — biopsy or patch testing sometimes needed; they can coexist), tinea (scrape), KE, PPP, keratoderma.

**smoking cessation** (strongest modifiable factor; refer to stop-smoking service/NRT); emollients; **very potent TCS** (clobetasol) ± occlusion overnight; salicylic acid for scale. Refer: hand–foot PUVA, **acitretin**, methotrexate, ciclosporin; biologics less reliable than in psoriasis. Screen thyroid/coeliac if symptomatic.

emollients and keratolytics (salicylic acid 2–5%, urea); **potent/very potent TCS** ± vitamin D analogue (calcipotriol) or combination products; occlusion overnight; lifestyle (smoking, alcohol, weight). Refer (CKS/NICE CG153): hand–foot PUVA, acitretin, methotrexate, ciclosporin, apremilast and biologics per NICE psoriasis TAs.

red_flags: Fever with sheets of pustules beyond the hands and feet: **generalised pustular psoriasis**, emergency.
Inability to work or walk: early dermatology referral.
Pustules on one foot only, or with interdigital scale: scrape for **tinea**.
pearls: Smoking cessation is the single most effective change in PPP; offer stop-smoking support at every visit.
Use very potent steroids under cling-film or cotton-glove occlusion at night for short periods, then step down.
Tell patients the pustules are **sterile**: antibiotics do not help.
Screen for psoriatic arthritis (PEST) and ask about chest-wall pain (SAPHO).

references.label: NICE CG153: Psoriasis: assessment and management
